records.text:
Histopathology:   - Tissue fragments showed necrosis of the dermal and superficial subcutaneous tissue with dense mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate and necrotic occlusion of blood vessels  - Periodic acid–Schiff stain revealed abundant thin, septate hyphae on the base of the ulcer and in lumen of necrotic blood vessels  - Fontana-Masson stain revealed no pigmentation of fungal elements
Mycology:  - Fungal culture showed colonies with white aerial mycelia, cylindrical conidia, and pigmented clavate appressoria  - Sequence analysis showed similarities with ITS1 (100% similarity, 171/171 bp), ITS2 (99.4% similarity, 156/157 bp), and D1-D2 domain (100% similarity, 553/553 bp)

bindings.label: Painful swelling over the right lower leg for 1 week
A woman in her 70s with a history of recurrent stasis dermatitis treated with long-term topical and systemic corticosteroids
She recalled being traumatized by plants on her right lower leg 3 months before presentation; she grows plants, especially orchids, inside her bedroom and on the balcony
Physical examination showed necrotic ulcers covered by hemorrhagic crusts and purulent debris on the right lower leg; she was afebrile
Biopsy reveals necrotic dermis with mixed inflammation, vascular necrosis, and abundant septate hyphae in vessel lumens
Fungal culture confirms a filamentous fungus with appressoria and high ITS similarity
PAS stain shows abundant thin-walled septate hyphae; Fontana-Masson stain is negative for melanin
Histological examination shows no evidence of malignancy
Post-traumatic angioinvasive fungal infection of the right lower leg
Bacterial culture of the right lower leg ulcer was not performed
MRI/CT imaging of the right lower leg was not performed
Histology shows necrotic vessel occlusion with septate hyphae
Secondary bacterial infection of the right lower leg ulcer
Deep extension of fungal infection in the right lower leg
